title: Matched-seed TTS listening comparison: 5 English and 5 Spanish phrases
quantization: Native GPTQ-Pro W4 G64 selective language backbone overlay, 142 modules
hardware: One free RTX 3090 (GPU 0), BF16 and INT4 resident together

generation_config.system: Perform TTS in American English / Spanish using a female voice

audio.ab_composite: RMS matched toward -23 dBFS, peak ceiling 0.88, MP3 128k and OGG Opus
audio.individual_stems: No gain adjustment; lossy Opus OGG from original generated WAV (not PCM lossless)

quality_assessment: ASR roundtrip with the BF16 LFM3 model transcribing each generated A and B sample. Word overlap recall and string similarity are intelligibility proxies, not human MOS and not independent ASR.
acceptance_gate: All 10 paired samples passed word-recall >=0.60, string similarity >=0.54, duration checks and matched duration-ratio checks.
notable_es1: Spanish sample ES_01 has lower roundtrip recall in INT4 (0.714) than BF16 (0.929) and longer duration (7.68s vs 5.60s). Treat this as a caveat, not a subjective rating.
bias_caveat: The quality-check ASR model is BF16 LFM3; its evaluation may favor its own synthesized output.
limitations: Only 10 paired TTS phrases; no listener study, MOS, ABX or CMOS.
Same random seed does not ensure identical stochastic sampling outcomes when weights differ.
Not a measured voice-quality ranking or real telephone-call test.
Generation timings are one pass per sample, not reliable service latency benchmarks.
Raw stems are un-normalized in gain but lossy OGG compression; the PCM WAV masters remain local.
This TTS comparison is separate from held-out human FLEURS ASR WER benchmarks.
